facts.fact_text: On 12 October 2010 the applicant organised a peaceful demonstration near the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office between 11.30 a.m. and 12.40 p.m.
About twenty-five persons took part in the demonstration on 12 October 2010 near the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office.

During the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the demonstrators were standing on the pavement in front of the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office when the police told them that they should remain at a distance of five metres from the building.

During the demonstration on 12 October 2010, the demonstrators were standing on the pavement in front of the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office when the police told them that they should remain at a distance of five metres from the building.
The police's instruction to remain five metres from the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office would have forced the demonstrators to stand in the road and obstruct the traffic.

The police told the demonstrators that they could not stand on the lawn and should move away, which would have meant standing in the road again and obstructing the traffic, causing temporary traffic-jams.
The two police officers grabbed the applicant's arms and took him in the direction of the nearby police station.
Some of the demonstrators requested the police officers to show them their identification and started filming the incident involving the applicant being taken by the police officers.
After the demonstrators requested identification and started filming, the police officers let the applicant go.

On 13 October 2010 the Lviv Regional Administrative Court granted a request by the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council to prohibit the holding of the pre-announced demonstrations by the applicant's NGO 'Vartovi zakonu' as from 19 October 2010.

The Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 on the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations in the city of Lviv introduced the procedure for organising peaceful gatherings in the city of Lviv.

Item 7 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 provided that notification about a planned gathering had to be given at least two working days prior to the date on which it was to be held.

Item 14 of the procedure introduced by the Decision of the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council of 16 April 2004 specified that gatherings could not be held in the road (except street marches and demonstrations), on lawns and flower beds, or in front of the central entrance (not closer than seven metres) and other entrances of administrative buildings, nor in case of non-compliance with sanitary norms.

On 1 June 2011 the Lviv City Council annulled the decision of 16 April 2004 of its Executive Committee on the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations in the city of Lviv.

Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that citizens have the right to assemble peacefully without arms and to hold meetings, rallies, marches and demonstrations, after notifying the executive authorities and bodies of local self-government beforehand.

Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine provides that restrictions on the exercise of the right to peaceful assembly may be established by a court in accordance with the law, in the interests of national security and public order only, for the purpose of preventing disturbances or crimes, protecting the health of the population, or protecting the rights and freedoms of other persons.

In its decision of 19 April 2001, the Constitutional Court of Ukraine noted that the current legislation of Ukraine did not provide for a specific time-limit within which the executive authorities or bodies of local self-government were to be notified about planned meetings, rallies, marches or demonstrations.

In its decision of 19 April 2001, the Constitutional Court of Ukraine held that the provisions of the first part of Article 39 of the Constitution of Ukraine on timely notification to the executive authorities or bodies of local self-government about planned meetings, rallies, marches or demonstrations shall be understood to mean that organisers must inform the authorities in advance, that is, within a reasonable time prior to the date of the planned event.

The police's instruction to remain five metres from the building of the Lviv Regional Prosecutor's Office would have forced the demonstrators to stand in the road and obstruct the traffic.

The police told the demonstrators that they could not stand on the lawn and should move away, which would have meant standing in the road again and obstructing the traffic, causing temporary traffic-jams.
The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the applicant had ignored the lawful demands of the police to stop breaching the peace.

The Galytskyy District Court noted in its decision of 14 October 2010 that the applicant had refused to follow the police to their station but instead called the participants in the demonstration, who shouted and threatened the officers.

On 13 October 2010 the Lviv Regional Administrative Court granted a request by the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council to prohibit the holding of the pre-announced demonstrations by the applicant's NGO 'Vartovi zakonu' as from 19 October 2010.
By a decision of 14 October 2010, the Galytskyy District Court found the applicant guilty of committing the administrative offence of malicious disobedience to a lawful order by the police.

By a decision of 14 October 2010, the Galytskyy District Court found the applicant guilty of committing the administrative offence of breaching the procedure for organising and holding a demonstration.

The Galytskyy District Court sentenced the applicant to three days of administrative detention starting from 6 p.m. on 14 October 2010, with reference to the relevant provisions of the Code on Administrative Offences.
At around 6 p.m. on 17 October 2010 the applicant was released from administrative detention.

In his appeal of 18 October 2010, the applicant argued that he had organised the gathering of 12 October 2010 lawfully and that the first-instance court's conclusion that he had 'held a meeting without permission of the City Council' had not been based on law as no such permission was required by domestic law.

In his appeal of 18 October 2010, the applicant argued that the requirement of notification two days in advance established by the procedure for organising and holding meetings, rallies, street marches and demonstrations in the city of Lviv, to which the police referred in their reports on administrative offences, was not based on law.

In his appeal of 18 October 2010, the applicant maintained that, in the absence of any lawful restrictions on holding a demonstration, demands by the police to stop such an event could not be considered lawful.

On 13 October 2010 the Lviv Regional Administrative Court granted a request by the Executive Committee of the Lviv City Council to prohibit the holding of the pre-announced demonstrations by the applicant's NGO 'Vartovi zakonu' as from 19 October 2010.
The decision of the Lviv Regional Administrative Court of 13 October 2010 prohibiting the demonstrations was appealed against.
According to the applicant, on 13 October 2010 he was invited to the police station on the pretext that he had failed to appear at a court hearing to which he had been summoned.

According to the applicant, the applicant telephoned his lawyer on 13 October 2010 while at the Galytskyy District Police Station, but the lawyer was not allowed onto the premises of the police station.
According to the applicant, at 11 p.m. on 13 October 2010 the applicant was placed in a cell at the Galytskyy District Police Station.
According to the applicant, the applicant remained in the cell without food from 11 p.m. on 13 October 2010 until 3 p.m. on 14 October 2010.

On 14 October 2010, before taking the applicant to court, the police drew up anew the reports on the administrative offences of malicious disobedience to a lawful order by the police and of breaching the procedure for organising and holding a demonstration.
The applicant had no opportunity to study the case-file materials before the court hearing at the Galytskyy District Court on 14 October 2010.

During the hearing at the Galytskyy District Court on 14 October 2010, the court rejected the applicant's request to be represented by the lawyer of his choosing on the ground that the applicant was a human-rights defender and could defend himself.
During the hearing at the Galytskyy District Court on 14 October 2010, the court rejected the applicant's request to summon and question witnesses.
During the hearing at the Galytskyy District Court on 14 October 2010, the court rejected the applicant's request to examine a video made during the events of 12 October 2010.
